# AWS stdin expected-size reference

Captured from the actual locked AWS CLI 2.31.18 executable, SHA256
`87630ec5232080b737502f4098f4c9adbf820c01d23c63b62affcad50059ad0a`,
on Linux x86_64 on 2026-10-16. These are independent executable/wire
observations, not values generated by ESS.

Each command pipes the documented bytes into `aws s3 cp - s3://audit-bucket/key`
with `--expected-size`, `--no-progress`, `--no-sign-request`, an empty shared
config/credentials environment, metadata disabled, and a local raw HTTP fixture.
The fixture returns successful PutObject or multipart initiate/upload/complete
responses. Every case exits zero and the owned peer finishes.

The smaller/larger hints 2 and 4 both upload exactly `abc` with Content-Length3.
For multipart, input is 9 MiB of ASCII `a`, hint is100 GiB, and default classic
transfer settings send one9MiB UploadPart. The ordinary8MiB chunk would require
two parts: the larger hint doubles the planning chunk to16MiB. Captured method,
query, length and SHA256 are retained in reference.json; multipart initiation and
completion XML is fixture-owned. ESS may add its independently required final
HEAD verification; that does not change uploaded bytes or sizing semantics.

Native ESS pipe keeps its separately tested exact expected-size assertion.
